exact_statement: The three-variable one-point defect f = 1 - 2*1{x = x0}, with address set A equal to two of its variables and with any number of dummy variables added, lies in the two-address conditional-product class and has H(f)/I(f) = 16/3 - (3/2) log2 3 = 2.955889... > 40/17. Hence any constant C_2 with H <= C_2 I on the class satisfies C_2 >= 16/3 - (3/2) log2 3. More generally C_k >= M_(k+1), the largest H/I over (k+1)-variable Boolean functions.

With A = {1,2}, A^c = {3}; every law on one bit is product, and dummy coordinates are deterministic in every conditional law. For k addresses the condition is vacuous on k+1 variables.

For a fixed address pair, equality holds for exactly 32 functions at N = 4 and 48 at N = 5, each an embedded three-variable one-point defect containing both addresses.

exact_statement: p_max (H(p) - H_inf(p))^2 <= (1 - p_max) Var_p(ell). Equality holds when ell takes exactly two values and the smaller value has mass p_max; in particular for the spectral law of every n-bit one-point defect. So the point-defect calibration (H - H_inf)/I -> 4 of the A031 anchor inequality is reproduced, with equality, without Booleanity.

proof_source.text: X = ell - H_inf >= 0, q = P(X = 0) >= p_max, mu = E X. Cauchy-Schwarz on {X > 0}: E X^2 >= mu^2/(1-q), so Var X >= mu^2 q/(1-q) >= mu^2 p_max/(1-p_max).
